subject: [PATCH] futex: Avoid hash-bucket locking for mismatched waits

reviews.author: Thomas Gleixner
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the patch's lockless read/test approach degrades performance by 5-10% on certain microarchitectures, leading to increased lock contention and potentially negative effects on wakeup latencies.
reviews.raw_body:
Not really free. The user space access is not exactly cheap either
because CLAC/STAC are memory fencing to meet the SMAP guarantees.

I've tried that lockless read/test before and gave up when a
multi-waiter real world test case degraded by 5-10% depending on micro
architecture.

It's carefully written to minimize lock contention in order to optimize
wakeup latencies. The effect of the extra unlocked access and it's side
effects shifts the timing enough that it runs into significantly more
lock contentions than before.

So it might be great for your use case, but not so great for others.

Thanks,

        tglx

2026-08-07.patch_summary: This patch modifies the futex_wait_setup function to read the futex word before taking the hash bucket lock, reducing contention and improving performance. The change allows for a precheck of the futex value without acquiring the lock, which is particularly beneficial in scenarios where the futex words are frequently mismatched. This approach also simplifies the code by removing unnecessary lock acquisitions and waiter accounting operations. By avoiding hash-bucket locking for mismatched waits, the patch aims to reduce contention and improve overall system performance.

reviews.author: Thomas Gleixner
reviews.summary: Reviewer Thomas Gleixner disputed the patch's claim that get_futex_key() only faults in shared futex pages, pointing out that it also gets a page reference for private futexes using get_user_pages_fast().
reviews.raw_body:
That's a fairy tale:

       get_futex_key()
          ...
          // shared
          get_user_pages_fast();        // gets a page reference
          ...
          folio = page_folio(page);
          ...

       out:
          folio_put(folio);	       // drops the page reference
          
Thanks,

        tglx

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged a potential performance issue related to STAC/CLAC instructions on older Zen CPUs, but noted that Zen 5's AC renaming improves their performance and is not a memory-ordering instruction like LFENCE.

Author responded to concerns about the patch's performance impact, explaining that a deliberately modified version of futex_wait_timeout.c shows no wall-time regression and that the extra userspace read does not cause contention or additional work under lock.
reviews.raw_body:
My understanding from 86e6b1547b3d is that STAC/CLAC \u201cend up serializing
execution on older Zen,\u201d while Zen 5\u2019s AC renaming \u201cimproves performance
of STAC/CLAC a lot a lot.\u201d  Architecturally, they only change the AC bit.
They are not memory-ordering instructions like LFENCE. I am currently
testing on Zen5 which could be why I didn't see any wall-time regression
in futex_wait_timeout.c from [1].

---

futex_wait_timeout.c [1] deliberately makes every call take the two-read path
and doesnt show any wall-time regression. The extra userspace read ofcourse
introduces additional instructions, but it is not showing up in any metric what
I thought would be the worst case in real world metrics.

The precheck adds no work while hb->lock is held, so it won't cause any more
contention.

I have been trying to coming up with some example userspace program that
would be negatively impacted by this patch and can't. I am not sure how
multi-waiter case that you described can result in 5-10% degradation
as the extra read is not showing up in wall clock time and we are not
adding more work under lock. I am currently testing on a Zen5 system.
Could you share the reproducer, thread topology, measured metric, and CPU
model on which you saw the 5\u201310% regression?

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260805132831.2852771-1-usama.arif@linux.dev/

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: The author acknowledges that folio_put() does not guarantee the page stays available, agrees to fix the comment in a future version (v2) if the discussion in another thread is successful.
reviews.raw_body:
I will fix the comment if the discussion in the other thread hopefully
works out and there is a v2. folio_put() does not immediately evict the
page; however as you point out it removes the guarantee that it stays
available.

get_futex_key() has just resolved the shared page, so a non-faulting
read is "very likely" to succeed. If it doesn't, we get -EFAULT and will
then reach the existing locked check and continues to do what is done
without the patch.
